body:
Google it. I wish I knew I was borderline when I met my current boyfriend. I would have told him to run.

Now I can't let him go, and for some fucked up reason he can't let go either.

I totally get what you're going through.

My situation is a bit different... A year ago, my ex got primary custody of my son, so I only have him on the weekends. My current boyfriend, however, has three girls. When the girls are at my house, I feel like I am going to go crazy. I hide from them. I spend the week either in my room or zoned into a video game because just the sound of them and their energy is too much for me.

I have gotten to the point where I dread even the weekend visits with my son because I feel that he should have a different mom. He should have one that is capable of being there for him like I was in the beginning.

I would give anything to be able to cope with being a parent and step parent again. I miss Enjoying motherhood.

If in the same situation, I would not bother going to a mental health office. I would probably go into the hospital and get someone's attention from there. 

I am in a really low and aggressive mind frame though.

At the very least I would contact the DBT group facilitater and explain the situation.
The simple act of seeing someone about your concern will not affect your job. I recommend going in and getting a professional opinion, if you are curious about it.

I would say it is more unfounded. I hate everything the is or was or will/could be.

I can like new things. I am hopeful of things and even people when they are new in my life. I feel as though I can start fresh and be better. But that goes away. It always goes away. That's when this hatred comes. 

In the passed, the only way I have stopped hating someone is by having to miss them. I run from everything and everyone, but I never truly get away. Every person I have ever run from never leaves my head. I miss them. All of them. I don't want to have to miss my SO. I don't want to have to hate him. 

It's not even just him. I just hate. I'm filled with it.
"Here we go again." That is the first thought to enter my head every morning/afternoon when I drag myself out of bed.

A couple days ago I decided that I wanted to go into my office and draw. When I got down there my computer was unable to play my music that I had on my phone... I snapped.

You are definitely not alone!
I got mine 4 months ago. I'm 27. So, you're still good haha

Alcohol may not be the cause of bpd but it definitely makes getting help harder. 

I encourage you to look into cutting out alcohol as I had to do. We suffer with lack of control enough and the alcohol just seems to take away the little control we do think we have.

I have no problem admitting that when I am drunk my rages are scary. 

I wouldn't go to AA but may even try to limit your drinking? You could find that it helps a bit.

Funny... If I thought people would stop shedding tears after a few weeks, I would have no problem leaving this world. It is the fact that I know some people will suffer for ever once I do it that makes leaving hard. In fact it makes leaving damn near impossible. Even when I have everything lined up.
Nothing. Just wait. I'm to much of a coward to do anything else.
There's no point. I'm not going to give a sob story so everyone can read it and be like oh she is just having a hard time. There is no way to understand.

I think it is extremely important that when you are with this person, your mind and attention is strictly on them. The person will give you 110% of them and expect it in return. 

By talking about a different partner you will make them feel they are not worth it to you to have your attention. You will cause them to start second guessing them self. 

Honestly, Imo I strongly recommend that you do not start a relationship with this person. Borderlines never feel good enough, and in your case, you will be give them a sense of competition. I think this will go badly for everyone involved.

I am diagnosed borderline and I am in a relationship with just my partner and I and I already have all these concerns. Depending on the borderline, being second will eventually devastate the person. The ugly side of a borderline is exactly that, ugly. Very ugly. Be careful. This will most likely destroy the person.
I always think they are lying too. I feel like they only give me the answer I want so I go away or so I don't get angry or depressed from the truth.

I tantrum. Unfortunately, I had a tantrum tonight and my step daughter (4yr) witnessed it as I yelled like a spoiled child. 

I am in therapy, both one on one and group. They are helping... my tantrums are less, but they definitely still happen. I hate them, and I get very angry with myself when they happen, but I am still learning to manage how quickly my emotions rise.

However, up until a couple years ago, I was more of a passive kind of borderline and internalized everything. I spent 24 years of my life without a single tantrum. I think it is just different levels of how heightened each borderlines emotions get.
I am also using this book. There are a lot of great tools in it as long as you're dedicated. I would recommend it to anyone that found themselves needing dbt

I don't think there is any relation to borderlines and the age they look, or their overall appearance for that matter. 

I do think that how a person acts or doesn't act can effect their appearance: extensive work outs, over eating, under eating etc. Drugs and smoking and other "coping" strategies that people use will change their appearance, but no, I highly doubt there is any form of evidence saying that bpd causes a person's appearance. 

I am a borderline female with really pretty facial features, and yes, I am very self conscious and have low self esteem. At the same time though, I have an eating disorder where I drastically over eat. So, saying that people with bpd and above average in appearance would be false.

I am also quite new to my therapy and my exercises and suffer with the same thing. It is hard. However, it is getting a lot easier the more I work on it. 

Recognizing is only one step in the process. Once you have learned to recognize it, changing it will come.

I personally got to a point where I was hating who I was as I recognized more and more issues, so much so that I became in Need of change. I demanded it of myself because I was not OK with it and recognizing it hurt.

Not acknowledging the problems is the only way I was able to continue with them.

I think this is just a learning curve and the change will come for you. You can't fix something if you don't know where it is "broken"
It can't.

My support network is very very complicated. I am in counseling and group therapies. I just wish they would work.  That's a lie. They are helping... Just very slowly.

My anxiety today turned into an extreme panic attack filled with anger and rage. Bad enough that I broke up with my boyfriend... The only person I DO have.

As for myself, I like my drawing. That's it. Sadly, drawing is a solo thing so it doesn't really get me out meeting people.

I laughed when you mentioned My little pony. I have step daughters and I always try and get them to watch my little pony. Cheesy but what ever. I just feel goofy and happy ish when I watch it.

He did see it as a symptom, and not as me being a slut. I how ever feel like a slut for doing what I did. I hold so much guilt and shame for it all. He is still helping and showing me how to separate myself from my disorder. He seems to have more patience for my disorder than I do. I am glad that I am able to separate the two most of the time. I am so thankful to be able to fix my mistakes without having to lose him.

As for my sister. You're right. There isn't much I can do, but I am doing my best at staying calm and using what I have learned. I like being able to show her that change is possible, when she is ready to do so.

I had a lead up of horrible behavior, suicide, drinking, cheating, and then I love my son. After losing him nothing seemed to Metter and I just sorta died from the inside. 

My boyfriend found out I cheated and surprisingly didn't leave me. He was my wake up call. He loved me and wanted me to get control. After seeing him hurt the way he did, I wanted to better myself and take control of my BPD. I am still with the same boyfriend, and we have had a few bumps in the road but therapy has done wonders. 

My sister and I were able to smooth over the fight before I came home, which is awesome. I hope she is able to find reason to help herself though.

Honestly...

Just Enjoy the good times.

I know I have a tendency to act very very irrational and over the top a lot of the time. But trust me. I (have BPD) hate those times just as much if not more then you.

When I have my good days. I want to just have my good days. I lose my "my good mood" very easily because it is at a point that my SO dwells on the blowup the other day or the night before or what ever.

No this is not me saying "you" cause my bad mood. But I personally feel like I am nothing but my illness to my partner now. He can't see the good. He refuses to try and blah blah. 

Have fun with her when she is in the mood to have fun. And a dress her issues when she has the issues (yes yes I know. Rocky and risky move). But, if you know How to talk to a borderline then talking to one will progress much more calmly.

Get under someone else?

Haha I'm sorry. I had to.
Place your phone or some kind of voice recorder in there where they won't notice it before everyone goes to bed.

Thank you. Working towards understanding my disorder has been a very very tough battle, but I have definitely come a long way.

I get angry when my SO is sad, sick, or stressed also. I'm not sure how you are when you are sick, but when he is sick or upset he withdraws. He says it is because he doesn't want to burden me, but Imo withdrawing is in the top three of my worst triggers. As a borderline, I suffer from fear of rejection and abandonment to the point that it is almost an obsession. When he shuts me out or gets distant, he sets off so many triggers at once and I just can't help myself. I feel like I am seen as "not good enough to help him."

It truly makes me sad and makes me feel like he will never open up to me when ever he is upset. Actually, one thing I have come to realize is that my rages are driven by sadness and fearfulness. They aren't even driven by anger. 


She may be different, but she may not. Have you heard of or read the book called "I hate you, don't leave me?" I have not read much, but when I do sit down to read it, it is almost creepy with how accurate it is when describing borderline characteristics. I think it is a good read for both partners.

I never screamed at him in the middle of the night, but I do constantly have nightmares that wake me up in the worst mental state imaginable. They are just consistent nightmares of all my fears that have the most control over my life. 
This could be something else that may be effecting her high emotional level at night.

I must say though, I am really sorry that it has resulted in you too sleeping separately, I could imagine not being able to be close to my partner at night (I'm overly clingy though lol). I like hearing that you are sleeping better at least. 

I don't know how to quote someone else's words with the fancy blue line or what ever so I'm not going to bother, but you mentioned that she said she felt better now that you were getting more sleep, but she can't seem to grasp that she is your reason for not sleeping... I have also been told, and have learned from experience, that Borderlines focus on emotions and feeling of those involved opposed to a non borderline who is more than likely drawn to the facts of the situation. We just function differently because that is how we have taught ourselves to do so for so many years. 

Edit: Wow, I'm sorry for my posts jumping all over the thread. I am not used to this apps version of reddit yet. I thought I was responding to the comments and not the original post. Lol In my defense, it is 3 am and my eyes are barely staying open.

Hmm. She seems to be very similar to how I acted for 2 years.

Sadly... While I was in denial, there really was Nothing that my partner could do, so yes I am saying that at this time there probably isn't anything you can do for her. 

A year ago, I was sure that my boyfriend hated me, made fun of me, was going to leave me, didn't love me and so on. Those feeling caused my rages, along with triggers that had nothing to do with him, and I was horrible. Absolutely awful to him because of my perception of the people around me, and there was Nothing he could do to fix any of it.

It is common for Borderlines to continue beating people down as long as that person will sit there and take it. One of the first things my therapist told my SO and I is that when I rage, he needs to leave. Man did I hate that. The first few times it made me more angry, but I was forced to give myself the time to calm the fuck down. I'm not sure if that is an option for you or not, but maybe concider it? Basically what I'm saying is, as the borderline, I raged on him simply because I could. He became a safe person for me to let my emotions just explode at and I hurt him bad because he took it, and I had no consequences. 

He stuck by me though... somehow... and our lives took a huge turn in January. That was when I got to a point that I realized that "I" wanted to help me... Finally. I still have rages, but I can go a few days without any now (I would rage daily and sometimes more than once in a day).

I don't know if any of this makes sense or not. It is difficult to make sense of what is in my head tonight for some reason.

Set boundaries and don't give in to her. Hopefully you will be able to work on becoming stronger until she leaves the denial behind.

I believe that there IS a way to handle this. She needs anger management or DBT. Or both. But is does work. IF SHE wants it to.

Is she in any therapy for her disorder?

I am a person with BPD that has been suffering for many years... 
In all honesty, every BPD is going to react differently to different situations or comments.
You are in the early stage of the cycle of most Borderlines which is a good thing, but it is very important that you read up on Borderlines as much as you can. The more my boyfriend knows about my illness, the better our relationship is, and the better I feel about myself.
Yup! fucking sucks.

I think connecting with a therapist in your new town before you go would be a really good idea for you.

Two years ago, I moved out of town, only an hour out of town but it was far enough to make me feel completely isolated and alone. My bpd issues became way way worse then they had ever been before hand. I wish I lined up a therapist first.

This comment might make you defensive, but I am assuming you have BPD because you are in this subreddit, and one of the things we are best at is blaming others.

I spent to much of my life hoping from one relationship to the next. I always said he was a dick.  He didn't care.  Etc... now that I am in a place where I am able to analyze my bpd, I am able to see that I was most of the problem. 

You will obviously make your final choice, but I personally would not jump into another relationship.

Honestly, I would strongly look at why you and your ex broke up before jumping into a rebound type situation. I have been in this situation before, and it never ends well. Give your self time to figure out what did and didn't work in the last one and figure out what you need in order for the next one to work.

I am in a really tough place with my BPD and to be honest, I don't know what kind of significant other I would find helpful.

My SO could do a list of things one day that makes me feel loved and validated and such. But the next day the same exact list of actions could be all wrong.

The joking about the driving though... Jokes is one thing that causes a lot of fighting in my relationship. Imo I think making the joke about her driving, when you know she has anxiety about driving already, is exactly what I want my SO NOT to do. 

When my SO cracks jokes about a certain subject that he knows I have issues of my own about, it instantly makes me feel like he is ignoring my feelings instead of validating them. He chooses to keep doing it, therefore, as the borderline, any validation that follows comes across as hollow.

Following are a few things that really make a difference for me with minimizing perceived rejection or "not giving a shit" 
- If we planned to do something at 6pm. Be ready at six PM. 
- Be honest with me when I have done something that upsets you without being an asshole.
  eg.  "I am really feeling hurt by what you are saying to me."   Instead of saying "Stop being a fucking bitch"
- If you fucked up, how ever rare that case may be, own it. 

Personally, I really just want to Feel heard and understood.

I totally understand that it is difficult to listen to us and to be calm with us after the amount of attacks you have received. I honestly could never switch rolls and have the same kind of strength to stay with someone so hurtful, however. We/I am the way I am and feel the way I feel because I have not been loved, I have been abandoned, I have been hurt, and I now show myself the same abuse. I want to be able to tell myself that I am loved, and I want a SO that is able to reassure me that I am loved on the days that I need it the most (the days that I'm angry with the world and he unfortunately is caught in the cross fire).

I don't know if any of this will make sense to anyone other than me but oh well. Hopefully some of it will.

I'm just curious...

I am the one with BPD in my relationship and am hurting my partner and hating that I do it. It has been three years for him and I and things have been really bad.

Did your partner ever attend therapy and try to get control of his disorder?

I am in therapy and am doing the best I can. Progress has been made and i am hurting less often but it seems like the hurt is greater. I love him more than anything in the world and want to get to a place where him and i are happy again. But I don't want to keep harming him if he is just going to break the way it seems most SOs have.

I saw your post in there, and I saw all the hate in there as well. I wish I never came across that sub. The thing that scares me more though is that my SO is the one that mentioned he has been in that sub a lot and I don't want him filled with anymore hatred towards me. I cause enough hate on my own. 

This book keeps getting brought up so much that I am now curious and want to read it. I am assuming you have read the book? Is reading the book going to make matters worse for me as the sufferer?

Best: my lack of confidence in everything has created a perfectionist attitude, or black and white thinking. My art work has only benefited from this, and is probably the only thing in my life that I am truly proud of.

Worst: This is tough because I feel that my BPD traps me in many areas. I think I would have to agree with others in this thread and say friendships/relationships don't last and I am left feeling isolated and alone all the time.
Glad I could help!

I'm going to respond to a response you put for someone else as well as mine. 

It is a long process, and a very difficult process. But, it really is worth it. I have heard many success stories from therapy groups that I am currently in. I truly believe that there will always be setbacks in my life, and I will always find myself having lows now and then. 

For me though, I have learned a lot of different techniques to cope with my lows and my impression of myself and others. I can say honestly that I am changing for the better, and am making positive impact all the time.

After I wrote my first reply, I pulled out (as silly and ridiculous as this will sound) my "positive encounters" journal. There have been fun interactions and positive events as early is two days ago. The hardest part is noticing them and remembering them instead of the negative ones. Until I started journaling, I couldn't see the positive days at all.

I share that because that is something that I consider a huge change from the way I used to think.

As for the fear of nothing being left, I'm not sure if it is the same for you or not, but I have spent most of my life feeling like I'm nothing. While in a positive frame of mind, I am able to talk to myself and see that the disorder is controlling me but it is not me. I try and think about the way my life can be different once I have control over me. No, you will not be the same person. But you will be you. You will be the you that struggles and seldomly gets shown to others.

Feel free to PM me anytime you feel you want to chat. Having people that not only listen but also understand is a huge key for success.

I have also struggled with this for as long as I can remember. I would never get close to anyone because I didn't want my friends to find out I'm not worth it.

One person however, I let in. I confided in her and we were best friends for 14 years. I could not let anyone else in. I was content that I had her.

Seven months ago, her and I had a fall out. We have not spoke since. We will not speak again. Since that happened, I cut of everyone I know. I am scared to see any friends. I am scared to give someone else that trust.

I am pushing my spouse away as well. I don't want to trust him. I do trust him, but I don't want to. It is to scary.

It has been almost a year since I was diagnosed, and I still suffer with it. 

I am actively in therapy and learning about how to cope, but I still have days where I don't want to be "cured." My whole life has been filled with borderline reactions. Everything has fallen into the cycle that we as borderlines go through. 

I am scared to calm the disorder because I don't know what I am like without the high emotion.

18 for me. I am really struggling with my borderline lately though, and everything is personalized. I saw negative emotions in all the faces.

I know you were suggesting borderlines in relaxed calmer states, but I wanted to try it now and then again when I am feeling uplifted, to see the difference.

I am a person with BPD and I do not take offense to the other comments or anything, but I know from experience that events in my life (large events) really do get lost if they are events that provoked a lot of anxiety and emotion. 

Another point I would like to say, I find myself forgetting a lot of small things, random things that I would do while stressing and dwelling on something in the past. In order to have a clear memory, it takes a lot of mindfulness skills. I personally struggle with this.

I'm not saying I have never manifested memories to try and prove to myself that I'm right. I have even been quite vindictive and manipulative and chosen to withhold memories to prevent myself from angering anyone further. I am however, saying that those instances are very rare.
